clue.text: Matured during attempt to produce Hamlet, for example

indicators.note: something happening during another thing sits within its span, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: an attempt is a try
matured means grown old, aged

explanation.surface: An actor who has grown older finally gets the chance to stage Hamlet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Matured' looks like the definition of a well-seasoned actor; the definition is Hamlet itself, a type of play.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Hamlet is an example of a tragedy, a play ending in the hero's downfall.

clue.text: List of people employed to catch old chicken

indicators.note: to catch is to hold something within, so the list wraps round a letter

parts.note: a roster is a rota of staff
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A staff rota drawn up to round up an elderly hen.
explanation.definitionFit: A rooster is a male domestic fowl, a cockerel, so a kind of chicken.

clue.text: Miserable character has good backside

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good
the rump is the backside

explanation.surface: A grumpy person happens to have a fine bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: A grump is a bad-tempered, sulky person.

clue.text: Editor rejected verse translation of warrant

indicators.note: of here joins the translated letters onto the turned-back abbreviation
something rejected is sent back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: ED is the abbreviation for editor

indicators.note: a translation renders words into another form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of verse rearranged

explanation.surface: An editor turns down a translated poem.
explanation.definitionFit: To warrant something is to deserve it, to merit it.

clue.text: Litter born in outbuilding

indicators.note: in places one element within the building, so it is enclosed

parts.note: a garage is an outbuilding for a car
B is the abbreviation for born

explanation.surface: A litter of puppies or kittens arrives in the shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Litter born' suggests animals, but litter here is rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Litter is rubbish dropped carelessly, which is garbage in American usage.

clue.text: Short article by brother put into circulation

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: circulation moves things round, so these letters are turned into a new order

parts.note: BR is the abbreviation for brother
taken as written before rearranging

explanation.surface: A brief piece written by a monk is published.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put into circulation' reads as published, but only 'into circulation' is the signal, working on 'put'.
explanation.definitionFit: Abrupt means curt or brusque, so short in manner.

clue.text: Second rate paperwork not turning up in sport

parts.note: second rate means poor, bad
minutes, abbreviated MIN, are a written record of a meeting

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means reading from the bottom upwards, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: taken as written before turning

explanation.surface: Shoddy forms fail to arrive for a sporting event.
explanation.definitionFit: Badminton is a racket sport played with a shuttlecock over a high net.

clue.text: Grace in unusual style of classical architecture

indicators.note: an unusual style is an odd arrangement, so the letters are set in a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Elegance in an offbeat way of designing ancient buildings.
explanation.definitionFit: Grecian describes things in the manner of ancient Greece, whose temples define classical building.

clue.text: Infant has help running project enjoying fleeting success

indicators.note: running suggests things in motion and loose, so the letters move into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A toddler gets assistance with a scheme that briefly takes off.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names something that shows early promise but quickly fizzles, from a musket's priming powder igniting without firing.

clue.text: Time flying saucer returned bland foodstuff?

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so these letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a flying saucer is an unidentified flying object

explanation.surface: A sci-fi tale of a spaceship coming back, ending oddly on food.
explanation.definitionFit: Tofu is bean curd, a soya product known for having little flavour of its own.

clue.text: Tout removing large household appliances from London store

indicators.note: removing takes something away, so a letter is dropped from the word for tout

parts.note: to tout is to sell, especially aggressively
L is the abbreviation for large
fridges are kitchen appliances

explanation.surface: A salesman clears out his big kitchen goods from a famous shop.
explanation.walkthrough: One L comes off SELL, leaving SEL. Selfridges is a large department store on Oxford Street.
explanation.definitionFit: Selfridges is a famous department store in central London, opened in 1909.

clue.text: US port strangely in a state of inertia

indicators.note: strangely means in an odd way, so the letters appear in an odd order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An American harbour town is oddly sluggish.
explanation.definitionFit: A stupor is a dazed condition of near unconsciousness, where one cannot act or move.

clue.text: Disease caught by clumsy Philistines?

indicators.note: caught by means held inside, so the letters sit within the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run from the end of the first word into the second

explanation.surface: A jibe that the clumsy Philistines picked up an unpleasant illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Syphilis is a sexually transmitted bacterial infection, a classic named illness.

clue.text: Bar found by high ranking officials visiting lake

indicators.note: someone visiting is beside the place they call on, so one piece is placed next to the other

parts.note: top brass are senior officers
Lake Erie is one of the Great Lakes

explanation.surface: Senior officers on a lakeside trip discover a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A brasserie is an informal restaurant or bar serving drinks and simple food.

clue.text: Checked the progress of beginner in unfamiliar department

indicators.note: in places the beginner inside the word for unfamiliar

parts.note: unfamiliar means strange
L is for learner, as on a British learner driver's L-plate
D is the abbreviation for department

explanation.surface: A new starter in a strange office has their advancement held back.
explanation.walkthrough: L goes inside STRANGE before the final E, then D is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Strangled can mean stifled or suppressed, as an idea strangled at birth.

clue.text: A shade of make up

parts.note: taken as written
a tone is a shade of colour

explanation.surface: A particular colour of cosmetics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make up' looks like cosmetics, but it is the verb meaning to compensate.
explanation.definitionFit: To make up for a wrong is to atone, to give amends.

clue.text: Stop the progress of wild boar next to front of tent

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter, which is added on here
wild means out of control, so these letters run loose into a new order

parts.note: taken as written before rearranging
the first letter of tent

explanation.surface: A wild pig by the campsite brings things to a halt.
explanation.definitionFit: To abort a plan or mission is to call it off before it is complete.

clue.text: So-called dividing line for resident scholar

indicators.note: so-called refers to what something is called, its spoken name, so the word is matched by sound

parts.note: a border is a line dividing two areas

explanation.surface: A frontier is nicknamed after a live-in student.
explanation.definitionFit: A boarder is a pupil who lives at school during term rather than going home.

clue.text: Spice stains are messy

indicators.note: messy means in disorder, so the letters come out jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A warning that this cooking spice leaves marks.
explanation.definitionFit: Star anise is the star-shaped dried fruit of a Chinese tree, used as a spice with an aniseed flavour.

clue.text: Stand in for monarch swallowing a substance used by chemists

indicators.note: swallowing takes something inside, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: a regent rules on behalf of a monarch
taken as written

explanation.surface: A stand-in ruler gulps down something from the lab.
explanation.definitionFit: A reagent is a chemical added to cause or detect a reaction.

clue.text: Prepared sushi containing Newfoundland variety of black bass

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so the abbreviation goes within the rearranged letters
food that is prepared is worked over, so these letters are reorganised

parts.note: taken as written before rearranging
NF is the abbreviation for Newfoundland

explanation.surface: A sushi dish made from a Canadian kind of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: In North America sunfish is a family name taking in the black basses, freshwater game fish.

clue.text: Prison officers detaining sailors in ship

indicators.note: detaining holds someone in, so one word is kept inside another

parts.note: SS is short for steamship
a crew is a ship's sailors

explanation.surface: Jail guards are holding seamen aboard a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: Screws is British slang for prison warders.
explanation.definitionFit: Screw is British prison slang for a warder or guard.

clue.text: Creature in farm building spinning lace

parts.note: a barn is a farm building

indicators.note: spinning things whirl round, so these letters are thrown into another order

parts.note: taken as written before rearranging

explanation.surface: An animal in the barn is busy making lace, like a spider.
explanation.definitionFit: A barnacle is a small marine crustacean that clings to rocks and ship hulls.

clue.text: Fiery pit depicted in painting

indicators.note: a thing depicted in a picture sits within its frame, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: painting is art
a den is a lair or hollow, a pit

explanation.surface: A canvas showing a blazing chasm, perhaps a vision of hell.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardent means passionate, burning with feeling, from the Latin for burning.

clue.text: Noise to suit dog?

parts.note: a din is a loud noise
to go with something is to suit it, as colours that go

explanation.surface: A dog trained to bark on cue.
explanation.definitionFit: The dingo is the wild dog of Australia.

clue.text: Grown up taking drug (speed), cut with inferior ingredients

parts.note: a grown-up is an adult
E is short for ecstasy
speed is rate

explanation.surface: An adult on amphetamines whose supply has been diluted with rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speed' looks like a second drug, but here it is simply rate.
explanation.definitionFit: To adulterate something is to make it impure by mixing in cheaper substances, as dealers do.

clue.text: Body part involved in common ailment

indicators.note: involved in means wrapped up inside, so the letters lie within the words that follow

parts.note: the letters straddle the two words

explanation.surface: Some part of the body is affected by an everyday illness.
explanation.definitionFit: A fingernail or toenail is a hard part of the body at the tip of a digit.

clue.text: Prim and proper priest getting a bit risqué?

parts.note: P is a dictionary abbreviation for priest
rudish means somewhat rude, a bit risqué

explanation.surface: A strait-laced clergyman starts telling slightly saucy jokes.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface contrasts a prim priest with naughtiness; P for priest is a less common abbreviation than PR.
explanation.definitionFit: Prudish describes someone easily shocked by matters of sex, overly concerned with propriety.

clue.text: Alice's first cup to get smaller

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter only of the name

parts.note: the opening letter of Alice
a cup awarded as a prize is a trophy

explanation.surface: Alice in Wonderland drinks from a cup and shrinks.
explanation.definitionFit: To atrophy is to waste away, as an unused muscle shrinks.
